clue.text: Old man injecting drug fix once ready

indicators.note: the old man takes the drug and the fix into his body, as with a syringe

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father
E is short for ecstasy
to set is to fix firmly in place

explanation.surface: An elderly man shoots up, needing a quick fix before he is ready to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash, so 'once ready' is money no longer in use; the Spanish unit was replaced by the euro in 2002.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'ready' means cash; this was Spain's currency before the euro, so it is money of former days.

clue.text: A third pic of one daughter looking humourless

indicators.note: a third of a three-letter word is its opening letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in a card game

explanation.surface: A photo of a daughter in which she looks grumpy.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal: someone po-faced wears a solemn, disapproving expression with no sense of humour.

clue.text: Rock and roller, in that context?

definitions.meaning: a hard piece of rock, a pebble or boulder
a rock that rolls, as in the band name The Rolling ...

explanation.surface: A query about whether rock and roll belongs here.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'context' is the band: a Rolling Stone is a rock-and-roller.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock is a piece of hard mineral, and rolling ones gave the band its name.

clue.text: Actor from Turkey, old chap

parts.note: TR is the international code for Turkey
aged means old
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: An actor from Turkey who is an elderly fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who specialises in tragic roles, or a writer of tragedies.

clue.text: Date surely problematic for Cotswold town

indicators.note: something problematic is in a mess, so the letters of surely are jumbled

explanation.surface: A date that is surely going to be awkward to arrange in a pretty English country town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cotswolds are a range of hills in south-west England dotted with stone-built market towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small market town in Gloucestershire, at the edge of the Cotswold hills.

clue.text: Old man went first, accepting wife moved slowly

indicators.note: the father figure takes the wife in, holding the letter inside

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
led means went in front

explanation.surface: An elderly man went ahead but, taking his wife along, slowed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dawdle is to waste time by moving slowly or idly.

clue.text: 21 breaking the law in foreign capital

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the law, splitting it apart

parts.note: a rule is a law
21 down is BISHOP, abbreviated B in chess notation

explanation.surface: Someone at 21 breaking the law in a foreign city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' means money, not a city: the Russian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian currency unit is money in a foreign land, so capital in that sense.

clue.text: Witnesses gangster leaving beauty salon

parts.note: a looker is an attractive person

indicators.note: the gangster leaves, taking his letters out of the word salon

parts.note: Al Capone was the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Witnesses see a gangster walking out of a beauty salon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lookers-on are onlookers, spectators who watch but do not take part.

clue.text: Joining together in greeting monarch

parts.note: yo is a slang greeting
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Joining in to welcome a king.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally putting a yoke on oxen, so linking or coupling things together.

clue.text: Young lad? He'll not need this!

definitions.meaning: an old informal term for a youngster or boy
a beardless youngster has no use for an electric razor

explanation.surface: A boy too young to need a razor.
explanation.definitionFit: A young boy is called a little shaver, and the same word names a razor he does not need yet.

clue.text: Portrayer of women, after a fashion represented here

indicators.note: the abbreviation for women comes after the rearranged letters
represented means presented anew, so the letters of 'a fashion' are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actress who plays female roles in her own way is celebrated in this puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle marks this Irish actress's 60th birthday; several other answers are women she has played on stage and screen.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish actress is a portrayer of roles, famous for playing tragic heroines in classic theatre.

clue.text: Director of British piece

parts.note: a rook is a piece in chess

explanation.surface: A film or stage director producing a British work.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Brook was a renowned English theatre director.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Brook was a celebrated stage director, famous for his Shakespeare productions and The Empty Space.

clue.text: Unattached detective's left Greek island

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the detective's letters go away from the longer word

parts.note: discrete means separate, not attached to anything else
DI is a detective inspector, and the 's gives 'is', so DI'S supplies the letters DIS

explanation.surface: A single detective has gone off on holiday to a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unattached' looks like a reference to a single detective; it is the word to be trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the largest island of Greece, in the Mediterranean south of the Aegean Sea.

clue.text: Supply 11, importing check fabric

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the word for check, bringing it inside
supply read as 'supple-y', in a pliant way, tells us to rearrange the letters

parts.note: the clue number is read as the word for the number, eleven
to vet is to check or examine

explanation.surface: An instruction to provide eleven lengths of checked cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: '11' looks like a cross-reference to the answer of 11 across; here it is just the number spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: A cotton fabric with a short dense pile that imitates velvet.

clue.text: Less reliable fellow? That's right

parts.note: dick is old slang for a fellow or chap
i.e. stands for 'id est', meaning 'that is'

explanation.surface: A query about whether some chap is untrustworthy, answered with a confirmation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' is British informal for shaky or unsound, as in a dicky heart.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang 'dicky' means weak or unsound, so the comparative describes something even less dependable.

clue.text: Grisly death? C-in-C took the risk

indicators.note: grisly means gruesome and mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A commander-in-chief who gambled and met a gruesome end.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to chance it is to take a gamble and hope for the best.

clue.text: End of old EMI's empire

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out of the run of words that follows, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: The record company EMI's empire has finally collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: EMI was a famous British record label.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a demise is a death or ending, as of a person or business.

clue.text: Service mostly average? Press for example

parts.note: Mass is a church service

indicators.note: most of the word is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: the median is a kind of average

explanation.surface: A church service that was mostly mediocre, according to the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the press is one form of mass communication, alongside television and radio.

clue.text: Thriller, first from Matthew Arnold

indicators.note: only the opening letter of Matthew is taken

parts.note: Arnie is the short form of the name Arnold

explanation.surface: A thriller as the first offering from the Victorian poet Matthew Arnold.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitchcock's 1964 film; Fiona Shaw sang the title role in an opera of it, so it fits the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's psychological suspense film of 1964, starring Tippi Hedren, is a classic of the genre.

clue.text: Play in Claret & Blue's last game

indicators.note: the final letter of blue is taken
game means willing to try anything, here signalling a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: A football match featuring a team in claret and blue, such as Aston Villa.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret and blue are the colours of English football clubs like Aston Villa and West Ham. CLARET plus E rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Sophocles' Greek tragedy, in which Fiona Shaw played the title role.

clue.text: As actor discontentedly simulated endless incest

indicators.note: dis-content-edly: with its contents removed, so only the outside letters of actor remain
simulated means faked or made up, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter of incest is dropped

explanation.surface: An actor grudgingly acting out an incest scene on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: As is the chemical symbol for this element; 'As' looks like a conjunction starting the sentence. The play 'Arsenic and Old Lace' adds to the theatrical picture. INCES rearranged gives SENIC.
explanation.definitionFit: As is the chemical symbol of the poisonous element with atomic number 33.

clue.text: Behaves badly, having drink after do

indicators.note: the drink comes after the word for do

parts.note: to act is to do something
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves after drinking at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a party; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a child or machine that acts up misbehaves or malfunctions.

clue.text: Golfer underclubs? Stupid mistake

parts.note: run together, 'under clubs' places the golfer below C, the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
Bernhard Langer is a German golfer, twice Masters champion

explanation.surface: A golfer chooses too short a club, a silly error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underclubs' is golf jargon for picking too weak a club; split it as 'under clubs'. A clanger is British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang: dropping a clanger means making an embarrassing, obvious mistake.

clue.text: One's bound to support black man going on board

indicators.note: in a down answer, a support goes beneath, so the other pieces sit under black

parts.note: one's read as I'S, I meaning one
a bound is a hop or jump

explanation.surface: A cleric tied to support a black man boarding a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, so he goes on a board.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the piece that moves diagonally is a man on the board.

clue.text: Beginning in Nice, tip poorly

indicators.note: poorly means badly done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone starting out in the French city of Nice tips the waiters badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something incipient is just starting to develop, like an incipient cold.

clue.text: Initially named Wilson, actor recently playing rising swimmer

indicators.note: in a down answer, rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
the opening letter of each of the next five words is taken

explanation.surface: An actor called Wilson has recently been playing a rising swimming star.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small shellfish that swims in the sea.

clue.text: The tragedy of some deaths

indicators.note: the answer is drawn out of the words that follow, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: The tragedy of several people dying.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'some deaths'. Euripides' tragedy is one of Fiona Shaw's best-known roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Euripides' Greek tragedy about the sorceress who kills her own children.

clue.text: Exercise? One needs a bit

definitions.meaning: military ... is exercise on the parade ground
a power tool for boring holes needs a bit fitted to it

explanation.surface: Exercise: something everyone needs a little of.
explanation.definitionFit: Repetitive training is exercise, and a tool for boring needs a bit.

clue.text: One way to score goal, say, with good skilful wing play

indicators.note: say signals that the word is heard rather than read: it is spoken aloud

parts.note: in football, a ball put in the net with the head is one way of scoring
able means skilful or competent
R stands for right, as in the right wing

explanation.surface: A football commentary on how to score a goal, with skilful play down the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like football, but it is the definition: Ibsen's drama, a famous Fiona Shaw role.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ibsen's 1891 drama about a restless, newly married woman, one of the great roles of theatre.

clue.text: Rolling Stones' second, then Radiohead? Flunkey wants Queen

indicators.note: only the second letter of the word Stones' is taken

parts.note: the head of Radio is its first letter, R

indicators.note: wants here means lacks, so the queen's letters are removed

parts.note: an underling is a flunkey or subordinate
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A music fan's ranking: the Rolling Stones in second, then Radiohead, with a lackey wanting Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The three bands are a smokescreen; 'Rolling' looks like part of the Stones' name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: trundling means moving slowly along on wheels, like a cart rolling.

clue.text: Bloomer affecting most of nuptial agreement, essentially

indicators.note: affecting means putting on or feigning, so the letters are rearranged
the final letter of nuptial is dropped
the essence of agreement is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A blunder that spoils most of a marriage contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a mistake, but it means a flower here. NUPTIA plus E rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering garden plant with trumpet-shaped blooms is literally something that blooms.

clue.text: See 26
